## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag needs an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment-variable default, which the project's CLI flag rules require for every new flag under `cli/`; this review found no other defect in the exclusion logic or its tests.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag that makes `collect` skip files whose basename matches any pattern, logging each skipped path. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds tests for parsing, filtering and archive output, and adds a text fixture under `tests/fixtures/`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — If CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log`, the archive still includes `.log` files, because `--exclude` uses `default=[]` and never reads the environment. `.claude/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5` (identical in `.agents/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5`) says: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI pipelines that set options through the environment, as the policy expects, cannot exclude files. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, split on a documented separator, add the variable to `docs/flags.md`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with an environment-set case.
